title: How to Create Your First Thrive Apprentice Course
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to set up Thrive Apprentice for the first time and create your first online course—from initial configuration to publishing your first lesson.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • The Thrive Product Manager used to install the plugin (available from your Thrive Themes account).

Accessing Thrive Apprentice

  1. Log in to your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Hover over Thrive Dashboard in the left sidebar menu.
  3. Click Thrive Apprentice.

Tip: You can also access Thrive Apprentice by navigating to the Thrive Dashboard page and clicking the Thrive Apprentice card.

Running the Setup Wizard

If this is your first time opening Thrive Apprentice, a setup wizard will appear automatically.

  1. Click Get Started on the welcome lightbox.
  2. Choose a page where your courses will be listed, or click Add New Page to create one. Then click Continue.
  3. Enter a name for your school design (e.g., "My School") and click Create new design.

Note: The page you select (or create) becomes your main Courses page—the public-facing page where visitors can browse all available courses. The design you create controls the look and feel of your entire online school.

Creating Your First Course

Once the setup wizard is complete, you'll land on the Thrive Apprentice dashboard.

  1. Click the Courses tab in the left sidebar.
  2. Click the Add course button at the top of the page.
  3. Enter a Course Title (e.g., "Introduction to Email Marketing").
  4. Optionally, add a Course Description to explain what students will learn.
  5. Click Save to create the course.

Your new course is now visible in the course list.

Adding Modules and Chapters

Modules and chapters help you organize your course content into logical sections.

  1. Open your course by clicking on it in the Courses list.
  2. Click Add Module to create a top-level section (e.g., "Module 1: The Basics").
  3. Enter a Module Title and click Save.
  4. To add chapters within a module, click Add Chapter underneath the module.

Tip: Modules are optional—you can add lessons directly to a course without modules if your content doesn't need that level of organization.

Adding Your First Lesson

  1. Inside your course (or within a module), click Add Lesson.
  2. Enter a Lesson Title.
  3. Click Save to create the lesson.
  4. To add content to the lesson, click Add content—this opens the lesson in Thrive Architect, where you can add text, images, videos, and other elements.
  5. When you're done editing, click Save Work in Thrive Architect, then click Done to return to Thrive Apprentice.

Publishing Your Course

By default, new courses are set to Unpublished status. To make your course available to students:

  1. Go back to the Courses tab.
  2. Click on your course to open it.
  3. Click the Unpublished dropdown in the top-right corner and select Publish.

Important: Publishing a course makes it visible on your courses page. You must have at least one published lesson or assessment before a course can be published. If you want to restrict access (e.g., paid courses), set up a Product with access rules before publishing. See the Access Restrictions and Rules guide for details.

That's it! You've successfully created your first Thrive Apprentice course, added modules and lessons, and published it for your students.

title: How to Use Course Content Types, Navigation, and Progress Tracking in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to organize your Thrive Apprentice courses using the four content types, understand how navigation works for your students, and see how the progress section tracks their advancement through your course material.

Understanding the Four Content Types

Thrive Apprentice uses a hierarchical structure with four content types that let you organize your course material from broad to specific:

  • Course — The top-level container that holds all of your content. Every piece of material lives inside a course.
  • Module — An optional organizational layer that groups related chapters or lessons together (e.g., "Module 1: The Basics").
  • Chapter — A sub-section within a module (or directly within a course) that groups related lessons together.
  • Lesson — The individual content unit where students consume your material—text, video, quizzes, and more.

Tip: You don't have to use every level. A simple course can contain just lessons, while a comprehensive certification program might use all four levels. Choose the structure that best fits your content.

Structuring Your Course Hierarchy

When building a course, think of the hierarchy as a nesting system. Here's how the levels relate to each other:

  1. Create a Course as the outermost container.
  2. Add Modules inside the course to divide it into major topics or units.
  3. Add Chapters inside modules to break topics into smaller groups.
  4. Add Lessons inside chapters (or directly inside modules or the course itself) for the actual learning content.

For example, a photography course might look like this:

  • Course: Mastering Digital Photography - Module 1: Camera Fundamentals - Chapter 1: Understanding Your Equipment - Lesson 1: Camera Body and Lens Basics - Lesson 2: Aperture, Shutter Speed, and ISO - Chapter 2: Shooting Modes - Lesson 3: Manual vs. Auto Mode - Module 2: Composition Techniques - Lesson 4: The Rule of Thirds - Lesson 5: Leading Lines and Framing

How Course Navigation Works for Students

Thrive Apprentice automatically generates a navigation sidebar for your students. This sidebar displays the full course structure—modules, chapters, and lessons—so students always know where they are and what comes next.

Key navigation features include:

  • Expandable sections — Students can expand or collapse modules and chapters to focus on the content they need.
  • Next/Previous buttons — Lessons include navigation buttons that move students sequentially through the course.
  • Clickable structure — Students can jump to any unlocked lesson directly from the sidebar.
  • Breadcrumb-style orientation — The current lesson is highlighted in the sidebar so students can see exactly where they are in the overall structure.

How the Progress Section Tracks Student Advancement

The progress section gives students a clear visual indicator of how far they've come and how much remains. Thrive Apprentice tracks progress automatically as students complete lessons.

  • Progress bar — A visual bar shows the percentage of the course the student has completed.
  • Completion checkmarks — Individual lessons display a checkmark once the student has finished them.
  • Module and chapter progress — Higher-level containers show aggregated progress based on the lessons completed within them.
  • Course-level overview — On the course overview page, students can see their total progress at a glance.

Note: Progress is tracked per student, so each logged-in user sees their own completion status. Students must be logged in for progress tracking to work.

Dynamic Labels That Adapt Based on Visitor Access

Thrive Apprentice uses dynamic labels that automatically change based on each visitor's access level. These labels appear alongside courses and lessons to communicate access status without any manual configuration on your part.

Depending on the visitor's permissions, they may see labels such as:

  • Free — The content is available to anyone without restrictions.
  • Login Required — The visitor needs to log in to access the course.
  • Purchase Required — The visitor must buy a product to unlock the content.
  • Restricted — The content is not available based on the current access rules.

These labels update dynamically—if a visitor logs in or purchases a product, the labels change to reflect their new access level. This keeps your course pages accurate and personalized without extra work.

That's it! You've successfully learned how to use the four content types to structure your courses, how navigation keeps students oriented, how progress tracking shows their advancement, and how dynamic labels adapt to each visitor's access level.

title: How to Create Course Bundles in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to create course bundles in Thrive Apprentice—allowing you to package multiple courses together and sell them at a single price point using the Products framework.

What Are Course Bundles?

A course bundle is a collection of two or more courses grouped together and sold as a single product. Bundles let you offer more value to your students at a discounted rate while increasing your revenue per transaction.

For example, if you sell three individual courses at $25 each, you could bundle all three together and offer the package for $60—giving students a $15 discount while earning more per sale than a single course purchase.

Understanding the Products Framework

In Thrive Apprentice, bundles are created through the Products section. A product is the mechanism that protects and sells your content. Products extend beyond just courses—you can use them to bundle courses with pages, posts, and custom content, making it possible to build entire membership websites.

Note: Every piece of content you want to restrict or sell needs to be associated with a product. Think of products as the "access keys" your students purchase to unlock content.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • At least two published courses ready to bundle together.
  • A payment integration configured if you plan to sell the bundle (e.g., SendOwl, WooCommerce, or ThriveCart).

Creating a Course Bundle Step by Step

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice in your WordPress admin.
  2. Click the Products tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Add New Product button.
  4. Enter a Product Name for your bundle (e.g., "Complete Marketing Mastery Bundle").
  5. Optionally, add a Product Description to explain what's included.
  6. Click Save to create the product.

Adding Courses to the Bundle

Once your product is created, you need to associate your courses with it:

  1. Open the product you just created by clicking on it in the Products list.
  2. Look for the Course Access or Content section within the product settings.
  3. Click Add Course and select the first course you want to include.
  4. Repeat for each additional course you want in the bundle.
  5. Click Save to confirm your selections.

Tip: You can also add pages, posts, and other custom content to the same product—not just courses. This is useful for including bonus materials, resource libraries, or exclusive blog content alongside your courses.

Configuring Access Rules

After adding courses to your bundle, you need to set up access rules so that only students who purchase the product can access the bundled content:

  1. Within the product settings, navigate to the Access Requirements section.
  2. Configure how students gain access—through a direct purchase, a membership, or a manual grant.
  3. Connect your product to a payment gateway if you are selling the bundle (e.g., link to a ThriveCart checkout or a WooCommerce product).
  4. Set any additional restrictions, such as time-limited access or drip-released content.
  5. Click Save to apply the access rules.

Important: When multiple access rules apply to the same piece of content, Thrive Apprentice uses a content protection priority system. The most restrictive rule takes precedence, so review your rules carefully to ensure students get the access they expect.

That's it! You've successfully created a course bundle in Thrive Apprentice, added courses to it, and configured the access rules that control who can unlock the bundled content.

  • Products Overview: Read more about using products in Thrive Apprentice to sell and protect content.

title: How to Create a Free Course Funnel in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to create a free online course funnel using Thrive Apprentice and Thrive Architect—a proven strategy for building your email list by offering a free course as a lead generation tool.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k4834OYrrNk

What Is a Free Course Funnel?

A free course funnel is a marketing strategy where you offer a free online course in exchange for a visitor's email address. Instead of selling the course directly, you use it as a lead magnet—attracting potential customers, growing your email list, and nurturing them toward purchasing your paid products or services.

Why Use a Free Course Funnel?

Free course funnels are one of the most effective ways to grow your audience because:

  • High perceived value — A free course feels more valuable than a simple PDF download, which increases opt-in rates.
  • Email list building — You collect email addresses from every student who enrolls, giving you a direct line of communication.
  • Trust building — Delivering quality content for free demonstrates your expertise and builds trust with your audience.
  • Upsell opportunities — Once students complete the free course, you can promote your paid courses, memberships, or services.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • Thrive Architect installed for building your landing page.
  • An email marketing service connected to your site (e.g., Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, ConvertKit).

Step 1: Create Your Free Course in Thrive Apprentice

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click the Courses tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Add Course and enter a compelling course title.
  4. Add a course description that highlights what students will learn.
  5. Add your lessons with the free content you want to deliver.
  6. Set the Course Status to Published.

Tip: Keep your free course focused and concise—three to five lessons work well. You want to deliver enough value to impress your audience without giving away everything you have to offer.

Step 2: Build a Landing Page with Thrive Architect

  1. Create a new page in WordPress (e.g., "Free Course: [Your Topic]").
  2. Click Launch Thrive Architect to open the visual editor.
  3. Choose a landing page template or start from scratch.
  4. Add a headline that clearly states the benefit of the free course.
  5. Include bullet points listing what students will learn.
  6. Add social proof elements if available (testimonials, student count, etc.).

Step 3: Configure Access—No Product or Payment Needed

Since this is a free course, you don't need to create a product or connect a payment gateway. You simply need to ensure students can access the course after providing their email:

  1. In Thrive Apprentice, make sure the course is not linked to any paid product.
  2. Set the course access to allow any logged-in user to view the content.
  3. New students will be created as WordPress users when they opt in through your form.

Step 4: Set Up the Opt-In Form

  1. In Thrive Architect, add a Lead Generation element to your landing page.
  2. Connect the form to your email marketing service using the API Connection settings.
  3. Configure the form fields—at minimum, collect the student's Name and Email Address.
  4. Set the After Submission action to redirect students to the course page or a thank-you page with a link to the course.

Note: Make sure the opt-in form creates a WordPress user account so the student can log in and access the course content in Thrive Apprentice.

Step 5: Connect Your Email Service

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > API Connections.
  2. Click Add New Connection and select your email service provider.
  3. Enter your API key or credentials and click Connect.
  4. Return to your landing page and link the opt-in form to the appropriate email list or tag.

Step 6: Test the Funnel

Before promoting your funnel, test every step of the process:

  1. Visit your landing page as a logged-out user.
  2. Submit the opt-in form with a test email address.
  3. Confirm you receive the email in your email marketing service.
  4. Verify the redirect takes you to the course or thank-you page.
  5. Log in as the test user and confirm you can access all course lessons.

Important: Test from an incognito or private browser window to simulate a first-time visitor's experience accurately.

That's it! You've successfully created a free course funnel that captures leads, grows your email list, and delivers valuable content to your new subscribers automatically.

  • Course Bundles: Learn how to create course bundles to package and sell multiple courses together.
  • Thrive Architect Landing Pages: Explore the Thrive Architect documentation for advanced landing page design.

title: How to Create a Student Profile Page in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to create a student profile page in Thrive Apprentice—giving your students a dedicated space to view and manage their account information directly on your website.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SekS3yGG3uA

Why Students Need a Profile Page

A student profile page gives your enrolled users a central hub to manage their account. Without one, students have no easy way to update their name, change their email address, or reset their password—leading to more support requests for you and a frustrating experience for them.

With a profile page in place, students can:

  • View their account details at a glance.
  • Update their name, email address, and password.
  • Feel more connected to your online school as a polished, professional platform.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • Thrive Architect installed for building and editing pages.

Understanding the Two Profile Page Types

Thrive Apprentice supports two types of profile pages, and you'll typically want to create both:

  • My Profile Page (Read-Only) — Displays the student's account information in a view-only format. Students can see their name, email, and other details but cannot make changes on this page.
  • Edit Profile Page (Interactive) — Includes the User Profile element from Thrive Architect, which lets students actively update their information, change their password, and modify their account settings.

Step 1: Create the "My Profile" Page (Read-Only View)

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Pages > Add New.
  2. Enter a page title such as "My Profile" or "My Account."
  3. Click Launch Thrive Architect to open the visual editor.
  4. Design the page layout to display the student's information. You can use dynamic text fields to show the logged-in user's name and email address.
  5. Keep this page read-only—do not add editable form fields here.
  6. Click Save Work when you're finished, then click Done to return to WordPress.
  7. Publish the page.

Tip: This read-only page works well as a dashboard-style overview that links to the separate edit page for making changes.

Step 2: Create the "Edit Profile" Page (Interactive)

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Pages > Add New.
  2. Enter a page title such as "Edit Profile" or "Account Settings."
  3. Click Launch Thrive Architect to open the visual editor.
  4. From the right sidebar, search for the User Profile element and drag it onto the page.
  5. The User Profile element automatically provides editable fields for the student's name, email, and password. Configure the element settings to match your preferences.
  6. Click Save Work when you're finished, then click Done to return to WordPress.
  7. Publish the page.

Note: The User Profile element allows your logged-in students to edit their user information, change their email, update their password, and more—all without needing to access the WordPress admin area.

Step 3: Add a Menu Link to the Profile Page

Once both pages are created, you need to make them accessible to your students by adding a link in your site's navigation:

  1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Appearance > Menus.
  2. Select the menu you want to edit (typically your primary navigation menu).
  3. Under Pages, find your "My Profile" or "My Account" page and click Add to Menu.
  4. Optionally, add the "Edit Profile" page as a sub-menu item beneath the main profile link.
  5. Click Save Menu.

Tip: You can also add a profile link directly within your Thrive Apprentice course templates or school design—so students see a "My Account" button while browsing courses.

That's it! You've successfully created a student profile page with both a read-only view and an interactive edit page, and linked them in your site's navigation so students can easily manage their accounts.

  • Thrive Architect Elements: Explore the Thrive Architect documentation for more elements and design options.

title: How to Use AI Course Generation in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to use Thrive Apprentice's AI Course Generation features to build and launch courses in minutes—whether you're starting from scratch or remixing existing content.

The AI Course Generation tool helps you overcome content creation paralysis by transforming you from a writer into an Editor-in-Chief. Instead of staring at a blank page, you let the AI handle the heavy lifting while you focus on adding your expertise and personal touch.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your website.
  • An active internet connection to access the AI generation services.

Generating a Course from a Prompt ("Prompt-to-Course")

The Prompt-to-Course engine allows you to generate a full course structure—including titles, modules, lesson headers, and content—from a simple text description.

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click the Courses tab.
  3. Click the Add Course button.
  4. Select Generate with AI.
  5. In the Topic field, enter a brief description of what you want to teach (e.g., "Beginner's Guide to Urban Gardening").
  6. Adjust the Difficulty and Course Length settings to match your target audience.
  7. Click Generate Course Structure.

The AI will create a proposed outline for your course. From here:

  1. Review the generated outline carefully.
  2. Regenerate specific sections or edit titles as needed.
  3. Once you are satisfied with the structure, click Generate Content to have the AI write the lesson summaries and text.

Tip: The more specific your topic description, the better the AI output. Instead of "marketing," try "email marketing strategies for small e-commerce businesses."

Remixing an Existing Course

The Course Remixer allows you to take a course you've already built and use it as a seed to create a new, fully written course for a different niche.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Find the course you want to use as a template in the Courses list.
  3. Hover over the course and select the Remix option.
  4. Enter the New Topic you want to adapt the content for (e.g., changing "Social Media for Realtors" to "Social Media for Dentists").
  5. The AI will rewrite the content, keeping the proven structure of your original course but adapting the terminology and examples for the new audience.
  6. Review the changes and click Save to create your new course.

Note: The remix feature preserves your original course—it creates a separate copy with the new content, so your existing course remains untouched.

Refining Your Course (Editor's Control)

You always maintain full control over AI-generated content. You are the Editor-in-Chief; the AI is your ghostwriter. Here's how to refine the output:

  • Regenerate Sections — If a specific lesson doesn't sound right, click the Regenerate button to get a fresh version.
  • Tweak Tone — Adjust the detailed settings to make the content sound more formal, casual, or enthusiastic.
  • Manual Edits — Edit any text field directly, just like you would in a regular WordPress post. This allows you to add your unique voice, stories, and expertise to the draft provided by the AI.

Important: Think of AI-generated content as a first draft that handles roughly 80% of the work. You should always step in for the final 20%—adding your unique anecdotes, real-world examples, and personal expertise. It is much faster to edit a solid draft than to write from a blank page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will the content sound robotic?

The AI produces a solid first draft, but it works best when you treat it as a starting point. Add your personal voice, swap in your own examples, and adjust the tone to match your brand. The result is content that sounds like you—created in a fraction of the time.

Is using AI for course creation "cheating"?

Not at all—it's efficiency. Just like using a calculator for math, using AI for drafting handles the repetitive structural work so you can focus on delivering high-value expertise and insights that only you can provide.

That's it! You've successfully learned how to use AI Course Generation to create courses from a prompt, remix existing courses for new audiences, and refine AI-generated content with your own expertise.

  • Course Content Types: Understand how to organize your courses with content types, navigation, and progress tracking.
  • Course Bundles: Learn how to create course bundles to package multiple courses together.

title: How to Use Dynamic Text in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to use dynamic text in Thrive Apprentice to display personalized, automatically updated content for each student—such as their name, course progress, lesson details, and module metrics.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D5-DbXb3ETc

What Is Dynamic Text?

Dynamic text is content that changes automatically based on the student viewing it. Instead of writing static text that looks the same for everyone, you insert dynamic text tags that pull in personalized information—like a student's first name, their completion percentage, or the number of lessons in a module.

For example, a lesson template with the dynamic text "Welcome back, [Student First Name]! You've completed [Course Progress]% of this course" would display as "Welcome back, Sarah! You've completed 45% of this course" for one student and "Welcome back, James! You've completed 80% of this course" for another.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • Thrive Architect installed (used for editing templates).
  • At least one course with lessons published.

How to Access Dynamic Text

Dynamic text is available through the Thrive Apprentice template editor. Here's how to get there:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click the Design tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the online school design you want to edit.
  4. Click the Manage Templates button in the Template Editor card.
  5. Find the template you want to modify (e.g., Lesson Template, Course Overview Template, or Module Template).
  6. Click Edit to open the template in Thrive Architect.

Inserting Dynamic Text Tags

Once inside the template editor, you can insert dynamic text into any text element:

  1. Click on a Text element in your template (or add a new one).
  2. Place your cursor where you want the dynamic content to appear.
  3. In the text editing toolbar, click the Dynamic Text icon (or look for the Insert Dynamic Field option).
  4. Browse the available dynamic text categories and select the tag you want to insert.
  5. The tag will appear as a placeholder in the editor—it will display the actual personalized content on the front end.

Available Dynamic Text Tags

Thrive Apprentice offers a variety of dynamic text tags organized by category:

Course Information:

  • Course Title — Displays the name of the current course.
  • Course Progress — Shows the student's completion percentage for the course.
  • Course Lesson Count — Displays the total number of lessons in the course.
  • Completed Lesson Count — Shows how many lessons the student has finished.

Module Information:

  • Module Title — Displays the name of the current module.
  • Module Lesson Count — Shows the total number of lessons in the module.
  • Module Progress — Displays the student's progress within the current module.

Lesson Information:

  • Lesson Title — Displays the name of the current lesson.
  • Lesson Number — Shows the lesson's position in the course sequence.
  • Next Lesson Title — Displays the name of the upcoming lesson.

Student Information:

  • Student First Name — Displays the logged-in student's first name.
  • Student Last Name — Displays the logged-in student's last name.
  • Student Display Name — Shows the student's chosen display name.

Walkthrough: Adding Dynamic Text to a Lesson Template

Here's a practical example of adding a personalized welcome message and progress indicator to your lesson template:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Design.
  2. Click Manage Templates and find your Lesson Template.
  3. Click Edit to open the template in Thrive Architect.
  4. Add a Text element at the top of the lesson area.
  5. Type "Welcome back, " and then click the Dynamic Text icon.
  6. Select Student First Name from the student information category.
  7. Continue typing "! You've completed " and insert the Course Progress tag.
  8. Finish with "% of this course."
  9. Click Save Work, then click Done to return to Thrive Apprentice.

Tip: Preview your template to see how the dynamic text looks with sample data. This helps you verify the layout before going live.

Note: Dynamic text tags only display personalized content for logged-in students. Logged-out visitors will see default or blank values, so consider using conditional display rules to hide personalized sections from non-logged-in visitors.

That's it! You've successfully learned how to access the template editor, insert dynamic text tags, and create personalized content that adapts to each student's progress and profile.

title: How to Switch to Thrive Apprentice From Another LMS
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to migrate from another learning management system to Thrive Apprentice—including a step-by-step migration checklist, platform-specific tips for switching from LearnDash and Teachable, and how Thrive Apprentice 4.0 features make the transition worthwhile.

Overview of the Migration Process

Switching from another LMS to Thrive Apprentice requires rebuilding your courses within the platform. You cannot directly import course content or structure from another system. However, you can export your existing students and import them into Thrive Apprentice—so your customers won't need to re-register.

Note: While rebuilding courses may sound like a lot of work, the process is straightforward when you follow a structured approach. The checklist below breaks the migration into seven manageable steps.

Why Switch to Thrive Apprentice?

Thrive Apprentice 4.0 introduced several features that make it a compelling alternative to other LMS platforms:

  • Products framework — Protect and sell courses, pages, posts, and custom content as bundled products, enabling full membership site functionality.
  • Drip content scheduling — Release lessons and modules on a schedule to keep students engaged over time.
  • Conditional display rules — Show or hide content based on a student's access level, progress, or login status.
  • Built-in design tools — Customize your entire online school's appearance without code, using the integrated visual editor.
  • No platform fees — Unlike hosted platforms, Thrive Apprentice runs on your own WordPress site with no per-student or transaction fees.

The 7-Step Migration Checklist

Follow these seven steps in order to ensure a smooth transition from your current LMS to Thrive Apprentice:

Step 1: Create Your Course Content

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click the Courses tab and create a new course for each course you're migrating.
  3. Recreate your modules, chapters, and lessons within each course.
  4. Copy and paste your lesson content from the old platform into each lesson's editor in Thrive Architect.
  5. Re-upload any media files (images, videos, downloadable resources) that were hosted on the previous platform.

Tip: Work through one course at a time to stay organized. Open your old LMS in one browser tab and Thrive Apprentice in another for easy side-by-side content transfer.

Step 2: Design Your Online School

  1. Click the Design tab in Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Choose a school design template or customize your own.
  3. Configure the layout for your course overview pages, lesson pages, and navigation elements.
  4. Set up your branding—logo, colors, and typography—to match your existing school's look.

Step 3: Set Up Products and Course Bundles

  1. Click the Products tab in Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Create a product for each course or course bundle you want to sell.
  3. Associate the appropriate courses with each product.
  4. Connect your payment gateway (e.g., ThriveCart, WooCommerce, or SendOwl) to handle purchases.

Step 4: Configure Access Restrictions

  1. Within each product's settings, define the Access Requirements.
  2. Set rules for who can access the content—paid students, free users, or specific membership levels.
  3. Review your content protection priority to ensure rules don't conflict.

Step 5: Set Up Drip Schedules

  1. Open the course you want to drip-release.
  2. Navigate to the Drip settings within the course.
  3. Configure when each lesson or module becomes available—based on enrollment date, specific dates, or completion of previous content.
  4. Save your drip schedule.

Step 6: Configure Login and Authentication

  1. Set up a Login Page for your students (or use the default WordPress login).
  2. Optionally, create a Registration Page if you want new students to sign up directly on your site.
  3. Configure any SSO (Single Sign-On) integrations if your old platform used external authentication.
  4. Test the login flow from a student's perspective.

Step 7: Import Your Existing Customers

  1. Export your student list from your current LMS (typically as a CSV file).
  2. In Thrive Apprentice, go to the Members tab and click the Import member button.
  3. Upload the CSV file containing your student data.
  4. Map the CSV fields to Thrive Apprentice fields (name, email, purchased products, etc.).
  5. Run the import and verify that students appear with the correct product access.

Important: After importing, send an email to your existing students letting them know about the platform change. Include their new login URL and instructions for accessing their courses.

Switching From LearnDash

If you're currently using LearnDash, the migration to Thrive Apprentice has a notable advantage: since both platforms run on WordPress, your student accounts already exist as WordPress users. This simplifies the process significantly.

Platform-specific tips for LearnDash users:

  • Student transfer is straightforward — You can pull in all your students from LearnDash to Thrive Apprentice without requiring them to re-register, since they already have WordPress user accounts on your site.
  • Content lives on the same site — Your lesson content (text, images, embedded videos) is already in WordPress, so copying it into Thrive Apprentice lessons is faster than migrating from an external platform.
  • Course structure mapping — LearnDash uses Courses, Lessons, Topics, and Quizzes. Map these to Thrive Apprentice's Courses, Modules, Chapters, and Lessons respectively.
  • Payment integration — If you used WooCommerce with LearnDash, you can continue using it with Thrive Apprentice for payment processing.
  • Deactivate LearnDash last — Keep LearnDash active until your Thrive Apprentice courses are fully set up and tested. Once you've verified everything works, deactivate the LearnDash plugin.

Switching From Teachable

Teachable is a hosted platform, which means your course content lives on Teachable's servers—not on your WordPress site. This requires a few extra steps during migration.

Platform-specific tips for Teachable users:

  • Export your student list — Teachable allows you to export your student data as a CSV file. Download this before starting the migration, as you'll need it to import students into Thrive Apprentice.
  • Download all media — Since your videos, images, and files are hosted on Teachable, download everything to your computer before cancelling your Teachable subscription.
  • Recreate course content manually — You'll need to transfer your lesson content by copying text and re-uploading media into Thrive Apprentice's lesson editor via Thrive Architect.
  • Redirect your domain — If you used a custom domain on Teachable, update your DNS settings to point to your WordPress site instead.
  • No per-student fees — One of the biggest advantages of switching is eliminating Teachable's transaction fees. With Thrive Apprentice, you keep 100% of your revenue (minus payment processor fees).
  • Maintain access during transition — Keep your Teachable account active until all content is migrated and all students have been notified of the change.

Warning: Do not cancel your Teachable subscription until you have exported all student data, downloaded all media files, and verified that your Thrive Apprentice courses are fully operational.

That's it! You've successfully learned how to plan and execute a migration from another LMS to Thrive Apprentice—using the 7-step checklist for a structured approach, with platform-specific guidance for LearnDash and Teachable users.

title: How to Set Up SendOwl with Thrive Apprentice (Legacy)
content:
Important: SendOwl integration is a legacy feature. Thrive Apprentice now offers built-in payment processing through Stripe and WooCommerce integration. We recommend using these modern alternatives for new setups. This guide is maintained as a reference for existing SendOwl users.

In this article, you'll learn how to set up the SendOwl integration with Thrive Apprentice—from creating your SendOwl account to configuring products, API keys, and course access protection.

What Is SendOwl?

SendOwl is a third-party digital product delivery platform that handles checkout, payment processing, and product delivery. When integrated with Thrive Apprentice, SendOwl processes payments and automatically grants students access to your courses after purchase.

Setting Up the SendOwl Listener

The SendOwl listener is the connection point between SendOwl and your WordPress site. It listens for purchase notifications and triggers course access.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Navigate to the SendOwl tab.
  4. You'll see a Listener URL—copy this URL.
  5. Log in to your SendOwl account.
  6. Go to Settings > Webhooks/Notifications.
  7. Paste the Listener URL into the webhook field.
  8. Save your SendOwl settings.

Important: The listener URL is unique to your WordPress installation. If you change your site's domain or permalink structure, you'll need to update the webhook in SendOwl.

Configuring API Key Permissions

Thrive Apprentice needs API access to communicate with your SendOwl account.

  1. In your SendOwl account, go to Settings > API.
  2. Locate your API Key and API Secret.
  3. Back in Thrive Apprentice > Settings > SendOwl, enter your API credentials.
  4. Click Connect to verify the connection.

Note: Make sure your API key has the necessary permissions for product management and order processing. Read-only keys will not work for course access provisioning.

Creating Products in SendOwl

Each course (or bundle) you sell needs a corresponding product in SendOwl.

  1. In SendOwl, go to Products > Add Product.
  2. Set the product Name to match your course title.
  3. Set the Price and payment options (one-time or subscription).
  4. Under Product Type, select Digital Product.
  5. Save the product.
  6. Back in Thrive Apprentice, go to Products and link the SendOwl product to the corresponding course.

Assigning Course Access and Protection

Once your products are linked, configure which courses each product unlocks.

  1. In Thrive Apprentice, go to the Products section.
  2. Click on the product linked to your SendOwl item.
  3. Under Course Access, select which courses this product grants access to.
  4. Configure Access Rules to restrict content to purchasers only.
  5. Save your changes.

Tip: You can assign multiple courses to a single SendOwl product to create a bundle deal—students gain access to all selected courses with one purchase.

The Purchasing Process

Here's how the end-to-end flow works once everything is configured:

  1. A visitor clicks a Buy button on your course page.
  2. They're redirected to the SendOwl checkout page.
  3. The student completes payment through SendOwl.
  4. SendOwl sends a webhook notification to your Listener URL.
  5. Thrive Apprentice receives the notification and grants course access to the student.
  6. The student receives a confirmation email with login details.

That's it! You've successfully set up SendOwl with Thrive Apprentice to sell and deliver online courses.

  • Modern Alternative — Stripe: Set up native payment processing with the Stripe Integration Guide.
  • Modern Alternative — WooCommerce: Use WooCommerce for flexible checkout with the WooCommerce Integration Guide.

title: SendOwl Operations and Troubleshooting (Legacy)
content:
Important: SendOwl integration is a legacy feature. Thrive Apprentice now offers built-in payment processing through Stripe and WooCommerce integration. We recommend using these modern alternatives for new setups. This guide is maintained as a reference for existing SendOwl users.

In this article, you'll learn how to manage day-to-day SendOwl operations—from customizing the checkout experience to managing customers, applying discounts, and troubleshooting common issues.

Managing the Checkout Process

Customizing Checkout Templates

SendOwl provides customizable checkout templates to match your brand:

  1. In SendOwl, go to Settings > Checkout Templates.
  2. Select an existing template or click Create New.
  3. Customize the layout, colors, logo, and text fields.
  4. Assign the template to your products under each product's settings.

Sending Customers Directly to Checkout

You can bypass your sales page and send visitors straight to the SendOwl checkout form:

  1. In SendOwl, open the product you want to link.
  2. Copy the Direct Checkout URL from the product's sharing options.
  3. Use this URL in your buttons, emails, or landing pages to send customers directly to payment.

Configuring the Registration and Thank You Pages

  • Registration Page — After purchase, students are prompted to create a WordPress account. Configure this in Thrive Apprentice > Settings > Login & Registration.
  • Thank You Page — Set a custom redirect URL in SendOwl under the product's After Purchase settings. Point it to a WordPress page with enrollment confirmation and next steps.

Managing Customers

Viewing the Customer List

  1. In SendOwl, go to Orders to see all completed purchases.
  2. Filter by product, date range, or payment status.
  3. Click on any order to view customer details, purchase history, and payment information.

Finding Specific Customers

To locate a specific customer:

  • Use the search bar in SendOwl's Orders section to search by name or email.
  • In Thrive Apprentice, go to the Members section and search for the student by name or email to view their course enrollment status.

Customer Login After Purchase

After completing a SendOwl purchase, students need to log in to access their courses:

  1. The student receives a confirmation email with login credentials (or a link to set their password).
  2. They visit your site's Login page.
  3. After logging in, they're redirected to their course dashboard with access to purchased content.

Tip: Make sure your login page URL is correctly configured in Thrive Apprentice > Settings > Login & Registration so students land on the right page.

Customer Login After Completing a Course

Students who return after completing a course will see their progress preserved. Course completion status, certificates, and grade data are stored in Thrive Apprentice—independent of SendOwl.

Mailing List Integration

You can automatically add SendOwl customers to your email marketing list:

  1. In SendOwl, go to Settings > Integrations.
  2. Connect your email service provider (Mailchimp, ConvertKit, AWeber, etc.).
  3. Map the product to a specific email list or tag.
  4. When a purchase completes, the customer is automatically added to your list.

Applying Discounts

  1. In SendOwl, go to Marketing > Discount Codes.
  2. Click Create Discount Code.
  3. Set the code name, discount type (percentage or fixed amount), and expiration date.
  4. Optionally restrict the code to specific products.
  5. Share the discount code with your audience—students enter it at checkout.

Viewing SendOwl Logs

SendOwl logs help you troubleshoot purchase and access issues:

  1. In Thrive Apprentice, go to Settings > SendOwl.
  2. Check the Connection Log for recent webhook events.
  3. Each entry shows the timestamp, order ID, product, and whether access was successfully granted.

Note: If a student reports they don't have access after purchasing, check the logs first. Common issues include webhook delivery failures, mismatched product IDs, or the student using a different email address.

Selling Subscriber-Only Courses

To sell courses exclusively to existing subscribers or members:

  1. Create a product in SendOwl for the subscriber-only course.
  2. In Thrive Apprentice, assign the course to this product.
  3. Set access rules so only users with the correct product access can view the course.
  4. Share the Direct Checkout URL only with your subscriber list through email campaigns.

Troubleshooting Common Issues

  • Student can't access course after purchase — Check SendOwl logs for webhook errors. Verify the student's email matches their WordPress account. Manually grant access in the Members section if needed.
  • Webhook not firing — Confirm the Listener URL in SendOwl matches the one shown in Thrive Apprentice settings. Test with a $0 product to verify the connection.
  • Duplicate orders — Check for duplicate webhook entries in the logs. SendOwl occasionally retries failed webhooks, which can create duplicate access records.
  • Checkout page not loading — Verify your SendOwl subscription is active and the product is published.

That's it! You've learned how to manage SendOwl operations including checkout customization, customer management, discounts, and troubleshooting for your Thrive Apprentice integration.

Related Resources

  • SendOwl Setup: Review the initial configuration in the SendOwl Setup Guide (Legacy).
  • Modern Alternative — Stripe: Migrate to native payments with the Stripe Integration Guide.
  • Modern Alternative — WooCommerce: Use WooCommerce for checkout with the WooCommerce Integration Guide.
  • Managing Members: Learn about member management in the Managing Members guide.

title: How to Navigate and Configure Thrive Apprentice Settings
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to navigate the Thrive Apprentice Settings page, configure general settings for your online school, and customize dynamic labels to match your brand's voice.

Accessing the Settings Page

To open the settings area, navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and click Settings in the left sidebar. This takes you to a centralized hub where you can manage every aspect of your online school's configuration.

Understanding the Settings Page Layout

The Settings page is organized into clearly labeled sections, each dedicated to a specific area of your Thrive Apprentice setup. You'll find the following tabs along the top or in the left-hand navigation:

  • General — Core settings such as your course page, URL slugs, auto-login, and comment preferences.
  • Login & Access Restriction — Controls for login pages, registration, and who can view your content.
  • Comments — Enable or disable comments on courses, lessons, and modules.
  • Email Templates — Customize automated emails sent to students upon enrollment, completion, and other events.
  • Assessment Uploads — Manage settings for student assignment submissions.
  • Labels & Translations — Adjust the default text and dynamic labels displayed throughout your courses.

Tip: You can jump directly to any section by clicking its name in the navigation. Each section saves independently, so you don't need to configure everything at once.

Configuring General Settings

The General tab is where you set the foundational options for your online school. Here's what you can configure:

Course Page Selection

Choose which WordPress page displays your Thrive Apprentice course catalog. This is the page visitors see when they browse all available courses on your site.

  1. Open the General settings tab.
  2. Locate the Course Page dropdown.
  3. Select the page you want to use as your main course listing page.
  4. Click Save to apply the change.

URL Slugs

Customize the URL structure for your courses, lessons, and modules. Clean, descriptive slugs improve both SEO and user experience.

  1. Scroll to the URL Slugs section in the General tab.
  2. Enter your preferred slug for each content type (e.g., courses, lessons).
  3. Click Save to update the URLs.

Important: Changing URL slugs after your site is live may break existing links. If you update slugs, set up 301 redirects for any previously shared URLs.

Auto-Login

When enabled, the Auto-login feature automatically logs users in when a new WordPress account is created for them. This provides a seamless experience for students who are added to your site through integrations or manual account creation.

  1. In the General tab, find the Auto-login toggle.
  2. Switch it On to enable automatic login for new accounts.
  3. Click Save.

Course Comments

You can enable or disable comments on your course content directly from the General tab. This lets students ask questions and interact with your material.

  1. Locate the Enable Comments for Courses option.
  2. Toggle it On or Off based on your preference.
  3. Click Save.

Using Dynamic Labels

Dynamic labels are adaptive text elements that automatically change based on the visitor's access status and context. For example, a label might display "Start Course" for a student with access and "Purchase Course" for someone who hasn't enrolled yet.

Where to Find Dynamic Labels

  1. Go to Settings > Labels & Translations.
  2. Select the Access Restrictions section.
  3. You'll see a list of customizable labels and call-to-action buttons on the right side of the screen.

Customizing Dynamic Labels

Each label corresponds to a specific scenario—such as free access, paid enrollment, or restricted content. To customize a label:

  1. Click on the label text you want to edit.
  2. Type your new text in the field provided.
  3. Repeat for any additional labels or call-to-action buttons.
  4. Click Save to apply your changes.

Here are some common labels you can adjust:

  • Free course label — Tells visitors the course is available at no cost.
  • Paid course label — Indicates that a purchase or subscription is required.
  • Call-to-action button text — The button text that prompts users to enroll, purchase, or log in.
  • Restricted content message — The message shown when a visitor cannot access course material.

Tip: Use clear, action-oriented language in your labels. Instead of generic text like "Access," try something more specific like "Enroll Now—It's Free!" or "Unlock This Course."

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to navigate the Thrive Apprentice Settings page, configure your general settings, and customize dynamic labels. With these fundamentals in place, your online school is ready for further customization.

title: How to Set Up Login, Registration, and Access Restrictions
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to configure login and registration pages, set up access restriction rules, manage what non-logged-in visitors see when they encounter restricted content, and register new users in Thrive Apprentice.

Prerequisites

  • At least one course created in Thrive Apprentice.
  • At least one product set up, since access restrictions are applied at the product level.

Understanding How Access Restrictions Work

Access restrictions in Thrive Apprentice operate at the product level, not at the individual course level. You create products that contain one or more courses, then apply restriction rules to those products. This approach gives you flexible control—you can bundle multiple courses into a single product and manage access for all of them at once.

When a visitor tries to access a course or lesson they don't have permission to view, Thrive Apprentice displays a customizable message based on the restriction settings you've configured. The Login & Access Restriction settings apply globally to all Thrive Apprentice products on your website.

Setting Up a Login and Registration Page

A dedicated login and registration page gives your students a clear entry point to access course content. Here's how to set one up:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Select the Login & Access Restriction tab.
  4. In the Login Page section, click Add a Login Page (or select an existing page from the dropdown).
  5. Customize your login page settings—including form fields, branding, and redirect behavior.
  6. In the Registration section, enable registration if you want new users to create accounts on their own.
  7. Configure registration fields and any welcome email preferences.
  8. Click Save to apply your changes.

Tip: Use the Thrive Architect visual editor to design a professional-looking login and registration page that matches your site's branding.

Configuring Access Restriction Rules

Access restriction rules determine who can view your course content. You can restrict access so that only subscribers, purchasers, or specific user roles can access your products.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Settings.
  2. Open the Login & Access Restriction tab.
  3. Scroll to the Access Restriction Rules section.
  4. Choose how you want to restrict content. Common options include:
  • Logged-in users only — Only users with a WordPress account can view the content.
  • Product purchasers — Only users who have purchased or been granted access to a specific product.
  • Specific user roles — Restrict access based on WordPress user roles such as Subscriber, Customer, or a custom role.
  1. Configure the restriction message that visitors see when they don't have access. This message can include a link to your login or purchase page.
  2. Click Save to apply the rules.

Note: These global restriction rules apply to all products. If you need different rules for individual products, you can override them at the product level by navigating to the specific product's settings.

What Non-Logged-In Users See

When a visitor who isn't logged in—or doesn't have the right permissions—tries to access restricted content, Thrive Apprentice shows them a restriction message. You have full control over what this message says and where it directs the visitor.

To customize the restriction message:

  1. Open Settings > Login & Access Restriction.
  2. Locate the Restricted Content Message area.
  3. Edit the text to communicate what the visitor needs to do—whether that's logging in, registering, or purchasing access.
  4. Optionally, include a link or button that directs visitors to your login page, registration form, or sales page.
  5. Click Save.

Tip: Keep your restriction message helpful rather than generic. Instead of "Access denied," try something like "This course is available to members. Log in or sign up to get started!"

Registering New Users

There are two primary ways to register new learners in Thrive Apprentice:

Self-Registration

When registration is enabled, visitors can sign up directly from your login/registration page. After registering, they receive a welcome email with their login credentials and can immediately begin accessing any courses included in their product access.

  1. Ensure registration is enabled under Settings > Login & Access Restriction.
  2. Verify that your registration page is published and accessible.
  3. When a visitor registers, Thrive Apprentice creates a new WordPress user account for them.
  4. The new user receives a welcome email with their login details.

Manually Granting Access

As an administrator, you can also manually add users and grant them access to specific products:

  1. Go to the Members section in Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Add Member or locate an existing WordPress user.
  3. Select the products you want to grant them access to.
  4. Save the changes. The user now has access to all courses within those products.

Important: When you grant access manually, the user must already have a WordPress account. If they don't, create one first under Users > Add New in your WordPress admin dashboard.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully set up login and registration pages, configured access restriction rules, customized restriction messages, and learned how to register new users. Your Thrive Apprentice courses are now properly secured and accessible to the right audience.

  • Member management — How to Manage Members in Thrive Apprentice
  • Course management — How to Manage Course Status and Bulk Actions

title: How to Manage Course Status and Bulk Actions
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to manage course statuses in Thrive Apprentice—including publishing, hiding, archiving, and scheduling courses—as well as how to use bulk actions to manage multiple courses at once.

Understanding Course Status Options

Every course in Thrive Apprentice has a status that controls its visibility and accessibility. Here are the available statuses:

  • Published — The course is live and visible to all visitors on your site. Students with access can enroll and start learning.
  • Draft — The course is not visible to anyone except administrators. Use this status while you're still building or editing your course content.
  • Hidden — The course is not listed publicly, but users with a direct link can still access it. This is ideal for exclusive or invite-only courses.
  • Archived — The course is removed from public listings and is no longer accessible to new students. Existing students who previously had access may still see it depending on your configuration.
  • Scheduled — The course is set to publish automatically at a specific date and time in the future.

How to Change a Course's Status

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar to view your course list.
  3. Hover over the course you want to modify.
  4. Click the status indicator or select Edit to open the course settings.
  5. Locate the Status dropdown and choose the desired status: Published, Draft, Hidden, Archived, or Scheduled.
  6. Click Save to apply the change.

Note: Changing a course from Published to Draft or Archived immediately removes it from public view. Students currently in the middle of a lesson won't be interrupted, but they won't be able to navigate to the course from the course listing page.

Scheduling a Course for Future Publication

The scheduling feature lets you set a course—or individual modules and lessons—to publish automatically at a specific date and time. This is perfect for drip content strategies or coordinated launch events.

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and open the course you want to schedule.
  2. Click the Content tab to view all modules and lessons.
  3. Hover over the Publish icon next to the lesson or module you want to schedule.
  4. Select Schedule from the options that appear.
  5. Set the date and time you want the content to go live.
  6. Click Save to confirm the schedule.

Once the scheduled date arrives, Thrive Apprentice automatically publishes the content—no manual action required on your part.

Tip: Scheduling works at both the course and lesson level. You can publish a course immediately while scheduling individual lessons to release over time—a great approach for drip-feeding content to your students.

Hiding Premium Courses from the Course List

If you offer premium courses that should only be visible to specific users or members, you can hide them from the public course list. This keeps your premium content exclusive while still allowing authorized users to access it via a direct link or through their member dashboard.

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Courses.
  2. Locate the premium course you want to hide.
  3. Change the course status to Hidden.
  4. Share the direct course URL only with authorized members or use your product access settings to control visibility.

Tip: Combine the Hidden status with product-level access restrictions for maximum control. Students who purchase or are granted access to the product will still see the course in their dashboard, even though it's hidden from the public listing.

Using Bulk Actions to Manage Multiple Courses

When you need to make changes to several courses at once, bulk actions save you significant time. Instead of editing each course individually, you can select multiple courses and apply changes in a single operation.

How to Use Bulk Actions

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Open the course you want to manage and click the Content tab.
  3. Select the checkboxes next to the lessons, modules, or chapters you want to modify.
  4. A Bulk Actions toolbar appears at the top of the content list.
  5. Choose the action you want to apply from the toolbar options.
  6. Confirm the action to apply it to all selected items.

Available Bulk Actions

  • Move — Relocate selected lessons or modules to a different chapter or position within the course.
  • Duplicate — Create copies of selected lessons or modules.
  • Delete — Remove selected items from the course.
  • Change status — Publish, unpublish, or schedule multiple items at once.

Important: Bulk delete is permanent. Double-check your selections before confirming a bulk delete action to avoid accidentally removing content you still need.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to manage course statuses, schedule future publications, hide premium courses, and use bulk actions to streamline your workflow. These tools give you complete control over how and when your course content appears to students.

  • Access restrictions — How to Set Up Login, Registration, and Access Restrictions

title: How to Manage Members in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn how to use the Members section in Thrive Apprentice to view member details, track enrollment and progress, remove members, and import existing members from a CSV file.

Accessing the Members Section

The Members section provides a centralized view of everyone who has signed up for or purchased your courses. To access it:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Members in the left sidebar.

You'll see a dashboard listing all your Thrive Apprentice members. This is your command center for managing student access, tracking progress, and maintaining your membership base.

Understanding the Members Dashboard

The Members dashboard gives you a clear overview of your student base. Here's what you can find:

Engagement Summary

At the top of the page, the Engagement Summary displays key metrics through a set of cards. Use the filtering options to narrow down the data by date range or specific courses. These cards help you quickly assess overall member activity and engagement.

Member List

Below the summary, the member list shows each individual member with the following details:

  • Name and email — The member's identity and contact information.
  • Enrolled products — Which products (and their associated courses) the member has access to.
  • Progress — How far the member has advanced through their courses.
  • Status — Whether the member's access is active or has been revoked.

Tip: Use the search bar and filters at the top of the member list to quickly locate specific members by name, email, or product enrollment.

Managing Member Access

From the Members section, you can perform several key management actions for any individual member:

  • Grant access — Add a member to a product so they can access its courses.
  • Revoke access — Remove a member's access to a specific product without deleting their account.
  • Unlock or lock content — Control whether specific lessons or modules are available to a member.
  • View progress — Check how far the member has progressed through their enrolled courses.

To manage a specific member's access:

  1. Click on the member's name in the member list.
  2. Review their enrollment details and progress.
  3. Use the available options to grant, revoke, or modify their access.
  4. Click Save to apply any changes.

Removing Members

There are different levels of member removal depending on your needs. You can revoke product access while keeping the user account, or remove the member entirely from your system.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cv5FIGaKZ_Q

Revoking Product Access

If you only need to remove a member's access to specific courses—without deleting their WordPress account—use the revocation method:

  1. Go to Members in the left sidebar.
  2. Find the member in the list and click their name.
  3. Locate the product you want to revoke access for.
  4. Click Revoke Access next to the product.
  5. Confirm the action.

The member's WordPress account remains intact, but they will no longer be able to access the courses in that product.

Completely Removing a Member

To fully remove a member from Thrive Apprentice:

  1. Navigate to the Members section.
  2. Find and click the member you want to remove.
  3. Select the Remove option.
  4. Confirm the removal when prompted.

Important: Removing a member from Thrive Apprentice does not delete their WordPress user account. It only removes their Thrive Apprentice membership data. To delete the WordPress account entirely, go to Users in your WordPress admin dashboard.

Importing Existing Members

If you're migrating from another membership platform, you can import your existing members into Thrive Apprentice using a CSV file. This ensures a smooth transition without requiring each member to re-register.

Step 1: Export Your Member List

Most membership plugins allow you to export your member database as a .CSV file. Export your list from your previous platform, making sure it includes at minimum:

  • Email address (required)
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Any relevant membership or product information

Step 2: Import the CSV into Thrive Apprentice

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Members.
  2. Click the Import button at the top of the members list.
  3. Upload your .CSV file.
  4. Map the CSV columns to the corresponding Thrive Apprentice fields (e.g., email, first name, last name).
  5. Select which products the imported members should have access to.
  6. Click Import to begin the process.

Thrive Apprentice will create WordPress user accounts for any members who don't already have one and grant them access to the selected products.

Note: If a member's email address already matches an existing WordPress user, Thrive Apprentice will link the import to that existing account rather than creating a duplicate.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to access the Members dashboard, manage member access, remove members, and import existing members from a CSV file. With these tools, you can efficiently maintain your student base as your online school grows.

title: How to Change the Lesson Type in Thrive Apprentice
content:
In this article, you'll learn about the different lesson types available in Thrive Apprentice, how to change a lesson's type, and when to use each format for the best learning experience.

Available Lesson Types

Thrive Apprentice offers three lesson types, each designed for a different content delivery style:

  • Text — A written lesson built using the Thrive Architect editor. Use text lessons for detailed explanations, step-by-step tutorials, downloadable resources, or any content that benefits from a rich text format with images, buttons, and other visual elements.
  • Video — A lesson centered around an embedded video. Use video lessons for demonstrations, walkthroughs, lectures, or any content that's easier to teach visually. You can still add supporting text below the video.
  • Audio — A lesson built around an embedded audio file. Use audio lessons for podcasts, interviews, guided meditations, or any content where students can listen on the go without needing to watch a screen.

Tip: You're not locked into your initial choice. You can change a lesson's type at any time without losing the content you've already added. The existing content is preserved—only the lesson's primary media format changes.

How to Change a Lesson Type

Follow these steps to switch a lesson from one type to another:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar and select the course that contains the lesson you want to modify.
  3. Open the Content tab to see all modules, chapters, and lessons.
  4. Hover over the lesson you want to change.
  5. Click Edit Details from the options that appear.
  6. In the lesson details panel, locate the Lesson Type setting.
  7. Select the new type: Text, Video, or Audio.
  8. If you selected Video or Audio, add the media source (e.g., a YouTube URL, Vimeo link, or uploaded file).
  9. Click Save to apply the change.

The lesson will now display in the new format when students access it.

When to Use Each Lesson Type

Choosing the right lesson type depends on your content and your audience's learning preferences. Here's a quick guide:

Text Lessons

Best for:

  • Detailed, reference-heavy content that students may want to search or skim.
  • Step-by-step instructions with screenshots or diagrams.
  • Lessons that include downloadable files, code snippets, or formatted tables.
  • Content that needs frequent updates—text is the easiest format to edit.

Video Lessons

Best for:

  • Visual demonstrations such as software tutorials or physical processes.
  • Lecture-style teaching where seeing the instructor builds connection.
  • Complex concepts that are easier to explain with animations or screen recordings.
  • Courses where engagement and completion rates are a priority—video tends to hold attention longer.

Audio Lessons

Best for:

  • Conversational content like interviews, discussions, or Q&A sessions.
  • Material that students can consume while multitasking—commuting, exercising, or doing chores.
  • Guided exercises such as meditations, language practice, or pronunciation drills.
  • Supplementary content that complements a primary video or text lesson.

Note: You can mix lesson types within the same course. A well-structured course often combines all three formats to cater to different learning styles and keep students engaged.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to change a lesson's type in Thrive Apprentice and when to use each format. Experiment with different lesson types to find the mix that works best for your content and your students.

title: How to Organize Lessons in Chapters
content:
In this article, you'll learn what chapters are in Thrive Apprentice, how they differ from modules, how to create and manage chapters, and best practices for structuring your course content so students can navigate it easily.

What Are Chapters?

Chapters are organizational containers within a Thrive Apprentice course that group related lessons together. They help you structure your content clearly so learners can navigate and progress through your course more smoothly. Think of chapters as sections within a book—each one covers a specific topic or theme and contains the individual lessons that teach that topic.

Chapters vs. Modules

Thrive Apprentice supports a hierarchical course structure with two levels of organization:

  • Modules — The top-level organizational unit. A module represents a major section or phase of your course. For example, in a photography course, modules might be "Camera Basics," "Composition," and "Post-Processing."
  • Chapters — A subdivision within a module. Chapters break a module into smaller, more focused groups of lessons. For example, under the "Camera Basics" module, you might have chapters like "Understanding Exposure," "Choosing Lenses," and "Shooting Modes."

The hierarchy works like this: Course > Module > Chapter > Lesson. You don't have to use all levels—if your course is simple, you can skip modules and organize lessons directly into chapters, or skip chapters entirely and place lessons directly inside modules.

Tip: Use modules for broad topic areas and chapters for narrower sub-topics within each module. This two-tier structure keeps even large courses easy to navigate.

Adding Chapters to Your Course

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar and select the course you want to organize.
  3. Open the Content tab.
  4. If you're adding a chapter inside a module, click on the module first to expand it.
  5. Click the Add Chapter button.
  6. Enter a name for your chapter—choose something descriptive that tells students what they'll learn in this section.
  7. Click Save to create the chapter.

The new chapter appears in your course structure, ready for you to add lessons to it.

Adding Lessons to a Chapter

  1. Click on the chapter to expand it.
  2. Click Add Lesson inside the chapter.
  3. Enter the lesson name and configure the lesson type (Text, Video, or Audio).
  4. Click Save.

You can also move existing lessons into a chapter by dragging and dropping them from another location in the course structure.

Reordering Chapters and Lessons

Thrive Apprentice uses a drag-and-drop interface to make reordering simple:

  1. Open the Content tab of your course.
  2. Hover over the chapter or lesson you want to move until you see the drag handle (the icon with horizontal lines).
  3. Click and hold the drag handle, then drag the item to its new position.
  4. Release to drop it in place.

You can reorder chapters within a module, move lessons between chapters, or rearrange lessons within the same chapter—all with drag and drop.

Note: The order you set here is the order students see when they navigate the course. Make sure the sequence follows a logical learning progression.

Renaming and Deleting Chapters

To rename a chapter:

  1. Hover over the chapter in the Content tab.
  2. Click the Edit icon (pencil) that appears.
  3. Update the chapter name.
  4. Click Save.

To delete a chapter:

  1. Hover over the chapter you want to remove.
  2. Click the Delete icon (trash can).
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

Important: Deleting a chapter also removes all lessons inside it. If you want to keep the lessons, move them to another chapter or module before deleting.

Best Practices for Course Structure

A well-organized course keeps students engaged and reduces dropout rates. Here are some guidelines:

  • Keep chapters focused. Each chapter should cover one specific sub-topic. If a chapter has more than 8-10 lessons, consider splitting it into two.
  • Use descriptive names. Chapter titles should clearly communicate what the student will learn. "Setting Up Your Workspace" is more helpful than "Chapter 1."
  • Follow a logical progression. Arrange chapters so each one builds on the previous. Start with foundational concepts and work toward advanced material.
  • Be consistent. Maintain a similar structure across modules—if one module uses chapters, the others should too. Consistency helps students know what to expect.
  • Don't over-nest. While the Course > Module > Chapter > Lesson hierarchy is powerful, not every course needs all four levels. Use only what makes sense for your content's complexity.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to create chapters, add lessons to them, reorder your course content, and apply best practices for course organization. A clear structure makes your course more professional and helps students stay on track from start to finish.
